title: Two weaknesses

D0.outcome: Explains that a second weakness stretches the defence beyond what it can hold.

D1.outcome: In a position with one weakness, names a way to create a second one and the pieces to attack both.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, chooses between pressing the first weakness and switching to a second, and keeps up pressure so the opponent cannot fix the first.

D3.outcome: Predicts when the siege on the first weakness should end because a second one has appeared.

misconceptions: Creating weaknesses is progress in itself.
conditions: If the opponent can fix his weakness, ensure a new one appears; force his heavy pieces to defend pawns.
There is a weakness attackable in two ways and the attacker's forces have more room.
contrasts: Creating weaknesses without a way to attack them.
Keeping up the siege after a second weakness has appeared.
A position with no weakness on either side.
